Title: Beaning Morning
Content: The summer `text(Sun)` rises up, peeking into my room.
Pulling up the soft sheet, I settle in for more sleep.
The season stretches out before me beyond sight,
Full of late mornings, hot afternoons, starry nights.
Dreams dance at the corner of my imagination until
Aunt Mary’s “Rise and shine!” races up the stairs.
I burrow deeper, hiding from the interruption.
The meaning shifts when she adds the magical words
“It’s beaning morning!”
A smile blossoms like a sunflower at `text(first)` light.
Forever ago, Aunt Mary and I had planted those seeds.
We’d watered, weeded, waited, watched as plants grew.
I imagined the green beans we would munch for `text(months)`
Tossed into salads, chopped into casseroles, served as sides.
I’d happily eat them fresh or steamed, pickled or canned.
`text(Each year)`, I dreamed of picking them alongside Aunt Mary.
Snapping the beans in `text(half)` was like a special summer song called
“It’s Beaning Morning.”
Early dew tickling my toes, I slip softly into the garden.
Aunt Mary walks gently beside me, the basket in hand.
The bean basket had been woven long before I was born,
Holding countless garden harvests grown over generations.
Juicy tomatoes sharing room with long zucchini, purple eggplant.
Summer `text(Sun)` and sudden rains changing soil and seeds into food.
The basket was like a treasure chest, carrying fortune for everyone.
Finally, at last, my favorite gem of all was ready, because
It’s beaning morning!
Like long green pencils, the beans hang down, silently waiting
For our skillful fingers to pluck and pinch them from the vine.
Yet, just as I reach out for the `text(first)` pod, Aunt Mary stills my hand.
She reaches inside the bean basket and pulls out a smaller basket.
A red ribbon encircles the handle; a paper tag announces my name.
Aunt Mary smiles as she hands the miniature bean basket to me.
“This is for today, tomorrow, and into the future,” she whispers.
“This is for every summer morning that you will greet by saying,
‘It’s beaning morning!’ ”
